section_summary: This section (pages 481-513) covers diplomatic and interdepartmental correspondence between the Japanese Embassy in Washington, the U.S. Department of State, and the U.S. Treasury Department concerning Federal income tax exemptions for Japanese government officials, naval technical officers, language students, and visiting scholars. Under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code and the Revenue Act of 1938, the State Department provided certifications of reciprocal tax exemptions granted by Japan to American officials, enabling Treasury to issue exemption rulings and instructions to local internal revenue collectors in San Francisco and New York. The documents include diplomatic notes requesting exemptions and reporting travel itineraries, State Department transmittals certifying reciprocity, Treasury approval letters, and administrative tracking forms.

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms that Japanese education scholar Hidetoshi Isobe is exempt from Federal income tax on his official compensation.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes responds to the Secretary of State's letter of March 22, 1939, regarding Hidetoshi Isobe, a Japanese national sent to the United States by the Japanese Department of Education for study. On the basis of the State Department's certification of reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938, the Treasury Department rules that Mr. Isobe's official compensation is exempt from Federal income tax. Appropriate instructions have been issued to the Collector of Internal Revenue and the Internal Revenue Agent in Charge in San Francisco, California.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter Granting Income Tax Exemption for Hidetoshi Isobe

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests Federal income tax exemption for naval language officer Engineer First Lieutenant Takeo Ito prior to his departure from Los Angeles.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests that Engineer First Lieutenant Takeo Ito, a language officer sent to the United States by the Japanese Navy Department, be included in the list of Japanese officials exempt from income taxes. The note states that Lieutenant Ito arrived in Washington on June 6, 1936, receives compensation solely from the Japanese Government, and is scheduled to sail from Los Angeles on April 24, 1939, aboard the steamship Kamakura Maru. The Ambassador asks that his status be brought to the attention of appropriate United States authorities.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 81 Requesting Tax Exemption for Takeo Ito

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State transmits Note No. 81 to Treasury and certifies reciprocal tax treatment for Lieutenant Takeo Ito.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr., a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 81 concerning Engineer First Lieutenant Takeo Ito, confirming a prior telephone message of April 22 to the Bureau of Internal Revenue. Hull certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants equivalent tax exemptions to American personnel and that Lieutenant Ito performs similar duties. He expresses the hope that Lieutenant Ito was exempted from Federal income taxation prior to his departure from Los Angeles aboard the steamship Kamakura Maru.
subfiles.title: Department of State Letter to Treasury Recommending Tax Exemption for Takeo Ito
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges Note No. 81 regarding Lieutenant Takeo Ito and confirms telephone notification to tax authorities.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 81 of April 22, 1939, regarding Engineer First Lieutenant Takeo Ito of the Japanese Navy. The note informs the Japanese Ambassador that the substance of his request was communicated by telephone on April 22 to the competent authority of the United States Government to ensure Lieutenant Ito's tax exemption prior to sailing from Los Angeles on the Kamakura Maru.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note Acknowledging Japanese Embassy Note No. 81

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests income tax exemption for civil engineer Juzo Ohtsuka before his departure for Europe.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests that Mr. Juzo Ohtsuka, a civil engineer with the Silk Conditioning House of Tokyo sent by the Japanese Government for study, be granted exemption from income taxes while in the United States. The note states that Mr. Ohtsuka arrived at San Francisco on January 12, 1939, has been residing in New York, and derives his income solely from the Japanese Government. He is scheduled to leave New York for Europe on May 12, 1939, aboard the steamship Europa.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 88 Requesting Tax Exemption for Juzo Ohtsuka

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State transmits Note No. 88 to Treasury and certifies reciprocal tax exemption for Juzo Ohtsuka.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr., a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 88 regarding Juzo Ohtsuka of the Silk Conditioning House of Tokyo. Hull certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan extends an equivalent exemption to American officials and that Mr. Ohtsuka's services are similar in character. He requests that Treasury instruct appropriate authorities to exempt Mr. Ohtsuka from Federal income taxation on his Japanese Government compensation prior to his departure on the steamship Europa.
subfiles.title: Department of State Letter to Treasury Recommending Tax Exemption for Juzo Ohtsuka
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Department of State acknowledges Note No. 88 regarding Juzo Ohtsuka and confirms transmittal to tax authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 88 of May 2, 1939, concerning the departure of civil engineer Juzo Ohtsuka on the steamship Europa. The note advises the Japanese Ambassador that a copy has been transmitted to the competent authority of the United States Government with a view to exempting Mr. Ohtsuka from Federal income tax on his official compensation.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note Acknowledging Japanese Embassy Note No. 88

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador submits a list providing the U.S. addresses of Japanese officials seeking tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: In compliance with the Secretary of State's note of April 29, 1939, the Japanese Ambassador transmits an updated list furnishing the addresses in the United States of Japanese officials seeking income tax exemption. These individuals were previously mentioned in the final paragraph of the list enclosed with Embassy Note No. 76 of April 14, 1939.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 89 Enclosing U.S. Addresses of Japanese Officials

subfiles.about: The Department of State forwards Japanese Embassy Note No. 89 with U.S. addresses of Japanese officials to the Treasury Department.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary of State George S. Messersmith writes to the Secretary of the Treasury regarding the exemption of Japanese officials from Federal income taxation, referencing State's letter of April 29, 1939. Messersmith encloses a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 89 of May 2, 1939, which supplies the U.S. addresses requested for the officials listed in the previous submission, supporting their certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.
subfiles.title: Department of State Letter to Treasury Transmitting U.S. Addresses of Japanese Officials
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department acknowledges receipt of the State Department's recommendation regarding Lieutenant Takeo Ito.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes acknowledges receipt of the Secretary of State's letter of April 28, 1939, enclosing Japanese Embassy Note No. 81 concerning Engineer First Lieutenant Takeo Ito. Hanes notes the State Department's certification that Japan grants equivalent exemptions to American personnel performing similar services. He states that the matter will be given careful consideration and that State will be advised of the determination as soon as possible.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter Acknowledging Recommendation for Takeo Ito

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests income tax exemption for naval construction inspector Constructor Lt. Commander Kitaro Matsumoto.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests that Constructor Lt. Commander Kitaro Matsumoto be granted exemption from income taxes while residing in the United States. Matsumoto, an Inspector of Construction of the Navy Technical Department, was assigned to the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspectors Office at 1 Madison Avenue in New York City. The note states that he arrived in New York on April 30, 1939, and that his compensation is derived solely from the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 97 Requesting Tax Exemption for Kitaro Matsumoto

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State forwards Note No. 97 to Treasury and certifies reciprocal tax exemption for Lieutenant Commander Kitaro Matsumoto.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr., a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 97 concerning Constructor Lieutenant Commander Kitaro Matsumoto of the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York. Hull certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants equivalent exemptions to U.S. employees and that Matsumoto performs similar duties. He requests that Treasury instruct internal revenue authorities to exempt Matsumoto's official compensation from Federal income taxation.
subfiles.title: Department of State Letter to Treasury Recommending Tax Exemption for Kitaro Matsumoto
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges Note No. 97 regarding Constructor Lieutenant Commander Kitaro Matsumoto.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 97 of May 4, 1939, concerning the income tax exemption of Constructor Lieutenant Commander Kitaro Matsumoto. The note confirms that a copy of the request has been transmitted to the competent authority of the United States Government to secure tax exemption for his compensation while serving at the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspector's Office in New York.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note Acknowledging Japanese Embassy Note No. 97

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador notifies State of the departure dates and vessels for three naval technical officers previously listed for tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador informs the Secretary of State of the scheduled departures of three officials of the Imperial Japanese Navy Inspectors Office who were included on the April 14, 1939, tax exemption list. Constructor Commander Masahide Iwasaki is scheduled to depart Seattle on May 29 on the Heian Maru; Assistant Engineer Shigeru Nagashima will sail from San Francisco on June 1 on the Tatsuta Maru; and Assistant Engineer Chuichi Itoh will depart San Francisco on June 24 on the Kamakura Maru. The Ambassador notes they were sent for study, are paid solely by Japan, and requests that their departures be brought to the attention of appropriate U.S. authorities.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 98 Announcing Departures of Iwasaki, Nagashima, and Itoh

subfiles.about: The Department of State informs the Treasury Department of the departure arrangements for naval officers Iwasaki, Nagashima, and Itoh.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary of State George S. Messersmith transmits to the Secretary of the Treasury a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 98 reporting the departure dates and vessels for Constructor Commander Masahide Iwasaki and Assistant Engineers Shigeru Nagashima and Chuichi Itoh. Messersmith notes that reciprocal tax certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code was provided in State's letter of April 29, 1939, and requests appropriate tax clearance instructions for the ports of Seattle and San Francisco.
subfiles.title: Department of State Letter to Treasury Regarding Departures of Iwasaki, Nagashima, and Itoh
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges Note No. 98 regarding the departure and tax exemption of Iwasaki, Nagashima, and Itoh.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 98 of May 4, 1939, regarding the departure from the United States of Constructor Commander Masahide Iwasaki and Assistant Engineers Shigeru Nagashima and Chuichi Itoh. The Ambassador is informed that a copy has been forwarded to the competent authority of the United States Government to ensure their Federal income tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note Acknowledging Japanese Embassy Note No. 98

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department acknowledges receipt of State's inquiry regarding income tax exemption for Commander Ko Nagasawa.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes acknowledges receipt of State Department letter of April 12, 1939, enclosing Japanese Embassy note of April 7 regarding Commander Ko Nagasawa, a language officer on a special mission. Hanes states that the request for Federal income tax exemption is receiving careful consideration and that the State Department will be promptly advised once a decision is reached.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter Acknowledging Request for Ko Nagasawa

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department acknowledges receipt of the general list of Japanese officials seeking income tax exemption.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John W. Hanes acknowledges Secretary Hull's letter of April 29, 1939, enclosing a list from the Japanese Ambassador of Japanese officials desiring income tax exemption. Hanes notes the reference to the Act of August 27, 1935, and the State Department's certification of equivalent reciprocity granted by Japan to American personnel. He indicates that the request is under careful review by the Treasury Department.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter Acknowledging General List of Japanese Officials

subfiles.about: A State Department file charge slip recording the borrowing of file 894.01B11 by Hendrik van Oss of Far Eastern Affairs.
subfiles.summary: This internal State Department charge slip records that file 894.01B11 was charged out to Hendrik van Oss of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE) on October 12, 1945. It documents postwar administrative access and custody of pre-war Japanese decimal records.
subfiles.title: State Department Charge Slip for Decimal File 894.01B11
subfiles.to: Hendrik van Oss, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador informs State of the departure of Professor Eisaku Kiso and requests income tax exemption, accompanied by a duplicate copy.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador notifies the Secretary of State that Mr. Eisaku Kiso, a professor at the Otaru Higher Commercial School sent to the United States for study, is scheduled to depart New York for Europe on June 21, 1939, aboard the steamship Europa. The note explains that Mr. Kiso was included on the May 2 tax exemption list, derives his income solely from Japan, and requests that his status be communicated to appropriate U.S. authorities. A duplicate carbon copy of the note is filed on page 507.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 99 Regarding Departure and Tax Exemption of Eisaku Kiso

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State transmits Note No. 99 to Treasury and certifies reciprocal tax exemption for Professor Eisaku Kiso.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr., a copy of Japanese Embassy Note No. 99 concerning Professor Eisaku Kiso of the Otaru Higher Commercial School. Hull certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants equivalent exemptions to American personnel and that Professor Kiso's educational mission is similar in character. He requests that internal revenue officials be instructed to grant Mr. Kiso an income tax exemption prior to his departure from New York on the Europa.
subfiles.title: Department of State Letter to Treasury Recommending Tax Exemption for Eisaku Kiso
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges Note No. 99 regarding Professor Eisaku Kiso and confirms referral to tax authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy Note No. 99 of May 5, 1939, concerning the departure of Professor Eisaku Kiso on the steamship Europa. The note advises the Japanese Ambassador that a copy has been forwarded to the competent authority of the United States Government to ensure Mr. Kiso is exempted from Federal income taxation on his Japanese Government compensation.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note Acknowledging Japanese Embassy Note No. 99

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department rules that architect Tatsuto Toki is exempt from Federal income tax for his work on the Golden Gate International Exposition.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury responds to the Secretary of State's letter of March 22, 1939, concerning Mr. Tatsuto Toki, an architect sent by the Japanese Government to supervise the construction of the Japanese pavilion at the San Francisco Golden Gate International Exposition. In view of State's certification of reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1938, the Treasury holds that Mr. Toki's official compensation is exempt from Federal income tax. Appropriate instructions have been issued to the Collector of Internal Revenue in New York.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter Granting Income Tax Exemption for Tatsuto Toki

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms that education language officer Takeo Watanabe is exempt from Federal income tax.
subfiles.from: Stephen B. Gibbons, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury Stephen B. Gibbons responds to the Secretary of State's letter of April 1, 1939, regarding Takeo Watanabe, a language officer of the Department of Education at Tokyo sent to the United States for study. Following the State Department's certification of reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, the Treasury confirms that Mr. Watanabe's official compensation is exempt from Federal income tax. Instructions have been issued to the Collector of Internal Revenue and the Internal Revenue Agent in Charge in San Francisco, California.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter Granting Income Tax Exemption for Takeo Watanabe

subfiles.about: An internal State Department memorandum noting telephone advice from Internal Revenue regarding tax exemption instructions for Mr. Yagi.
subfiles.from: V. Ellis, Division of Foreign Service Administration
subfiles.summary: This State Department memorandum by V. Ellis of the Division of Foreign Service Administration records that Miss Hines of the Bureau of Internal Revenue advised by telephone on May 10, 1939, that the Collector of Internal Revenue at New York City would be appropriately instructed concerning the tax-exempt status of Mr. Yagi.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum on Tax Exemption for Mr. Yagi
subfiles.to: Division of Foreign Service Administration File
